key_moves: Sequential arm placements ending in a hip swivel and quarter turn, repeated.
cultural_context: Spanish duo's flamenco-pop track that became a 1990s global wedding and party staple after the Bayside Boys remix.

key_moves: Galloping horse-riding motion with lasso arm and bounce.
cultural_context: Satire of affluent Seoul's Gangnam district; first YouTube video to reach one billion views.

key_moves: Mimed everyday gestures (ironing, driving, washing) over a hip-and-knee groove.
cultural_context: Accra street dance that spread across West Africa and the UK diaspora, popularizing Afrobeats abroad.

key_moves: Rapid circular neck rotation combined with a seated hip wine.
cultural_context: Jamaican dancehall move from the mid-2000s Kingston dance scene, controversial for neck-injury risk.

key_moves: Quick heel-toe footwork spelling shapes, originally gang-affiliated.
cultural_context: Born in 1970s Compton gang culture, later absorbed into mainstream hip-hop and pop performance.

key_moves: Fast arm waves, woah, and whip combination synced to the beat drop.
cultural_context: Choreographed by 14-year-old Jalaiah Harmon; became the defining TikTok dance and a credit-attribution case study.

key_moves: Crouched stomping with a circular leg-drag and rolling arm.
cultural_context: South African gqom-era move taken global after Rihanna and Childish Gambino performed it on major stages.

key_moves: Loose side-to-side sway with a hand brushing through the hair.
cultural_context: Named after 1980s rapper Doug E. Fresh; revived as a 2010 viral crossover hit.
